---

This scatterplot below shows the relationship between a car's weight (`wt`) and its fuel efficiency (`mpg`). @cr-plot1

Heavier cars tend to get fewer miles per gallon. [@cr-plot1]{pan-to="-25%,-25%"}

Lighter cars are generally more efficient. [@cr-plot1]{pan-to="25%,25%"}

::: {#cr-plot1}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

mtcars_plot <- mtcars |>
  mutate(cyl = factor(cyl))

ggplot(mtcars_plot, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = cyl)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.85) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Car Weight vs. Fuel Efficiency",
    x = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
    y = "Miles Per Gallon",
    color = "Cylinders"
  )
```

:::

---

Let's look at number of cylinders. The table below shows average horsepower, weight, and fuel efficiency for 4, 6, and 8-cylinder cars. @cr-table1

::: {#cr-table1}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false

mtcars |>
  group_by(cyl) |>
  summarize(
    `Average HP` = mean(hp),
    `Average Weight (1000 lbs)` = mean(wt),
    `Average MPG` = mean(mpg),
    `Count` = n()
  ) |>
  rename(Cylinders = cyl) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "html")
```
:::


4-cylinder cars are the clear winners in fuel efficiency. @cr-table2

::: {#cr-table2}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false

mtcars |>
  group_by(cyl) |>
  summarize(
    `Average HP` = mean(hp),
    `Average Weight (1000 lbs)` = mean(wt),
    `Average MPG` = mean(mpg),
    `Count` = n()
  ) |>
  rename(Cylinders = cyl) |>
  filter(Cylinders == 4) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "html")
```
:::

8-cylinder cars dominate in raw horsepower. @cr-table3

::: {#cr-table3}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false

mtcars |>
  group_by(cyl) |>
  summarize(
    `Average HP` = mean(hp),

  ) |>

```
